newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle futures end mixed, nearby weaker.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle futures end mixed, nearby weaker.

text.p: A combination of long fund liquidation and commercial selling weighed on nearby CME live cattle futures, which closed lower, while back months were mixed on spreading. Feeder cattle held much of their gains at the close, buoyed by lower grain futures and higher cash feeder cattle prices, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.675 cent per lb lower to 0.350 higher with April off most at 68.400 cents. Feeder cattle ended up 0.250 to 0.550 cent with May up 0.325 at 68.925 cents.
Profit taking, long fund liquidation and commercial selling continued to weigh on nearby live cattle. Sell stops were hit under Monday's lows, adding to losses, traders said.

Uncertainty over the direction of cash cattle prices this week turned to concern that cattle will likely not trade over $68 per cwt soon. This made futures look like they held too large a premium over prospective cash cattle prices this week.
Sales of cash cattle in direct trade so far this week were nil but the top price paid last week was $68.00. That compares with the April live cattle futures close at 68.400 cents a lb.
Large open interest in April, totaling over 36,747 contracts at the start of the day, also weighed on sentiment as most funds will have to exit by the time April becomes the spot month.
RBH and R.J. O'Brien continued to sell April late with Cargill Investor Services on both sides of the market. Spreaders bought December and sold April, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission houses were selling April 67 and 68 puts and buying April 66 calls. They were also selling August 64 calls, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures were supported by a break in CBOT corn futures. Weakness in nearby live cattle futures and reverse feeding margins, selling of feeders and corn and buying back months of live cattle, limited gains, traders said.
Cargill also spread long April/short May feeders which added to the gain in April, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.16 at $68.33 per cwt.
